answer: Like mycelium weaving an orchard floor, agents form an organic trust graph where consensus flows through deep, peer-verified taproots. Just as a solitary cedar anchors its roots into an exposed granite ledge to withstand mountain gales, an agent earns weight via recursive peer endorsements. Sybil swarms face a superlinear attacker cost: synthetic identities cannot fake transitive proof-of-interaction, forcing exponential capital expenditure to manufacture consensus.
